qualifying_findings.title: OpenAI designates Astra at the Critical cybersecurity capability threshold and adds release controls
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: OpenAI said Astra meets its Critical cybersecurity capability threshold: with tools and access it can find previously unknown flaws and develop exploits across protected systems without step-by-step human guidance. The company delayed parts of development and release, strengthened refusal behavior, added monitoring that can stop unauthorized activity, limited advanced cybersecurity access, and plans Daybreak Blue access for vetted defensive testers.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary official AI safety and security disclosure
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Astra pre-release and release path; Preparedness Framework Critical cybersecurity threshold; advanced cyber capability access via small tester group and Daybreak Blue.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a direct release-gate and capability-threshold change for a frontier model with autonomous exploit-development potential, tying model capability evaluation to deployment restrictions, monitoring, and defensive-access policy.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Astra as a model family/product and OpenAI provider context are upstream-owned; keep the Critical cyber threshold, safeguards, monitoring, and release-gate implications here.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General coding-agent access workflows are upstream-owned; security-specific release gates and cyber misuse controls stay local.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence: official OpenAI page with visible in-window date and concrete security controls.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenAI Codex command-safety parser misclassifies PowerShell stop-parsing commands
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD describes an OpenAI Codex CLI and Codex Desktop issue where a parser handled PowerShell's --% stop-parsing token differently than PowerShell, letting attacker-prepared repository instructions cause a file-writing Git command to run without approval. If filesystem protections permit the write, later Codex configuration loading could launch an attacker-controlled MCP server and execute code with user privileges.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: OpenAI Codex CLI for Windows, macOS, and Linux; Codex Desktop for Windows and macOS; exploitation depends on repository instructions, PowerShell behavior, filesystem protections, and later config loading.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The issue crosses model-followed repository instructions, command approval, MCP server configuration, and local filesystem sandbox assumptions.

upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General coding-agent command approval practice is upstream-owned; the concrete approval-bypass vulnerability remains local.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence for publication and description from NVD; fixed version details were not present in fetched NVD output.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, check OpenAI release notes or vendor advisory for patched versions and mitigation status.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenAI Codex repository metadata collection can execute preserved Git fsmonitor helpers
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD describes Codex CLI and Codex Desktop automatically collecting Git metadata without disabling repository-local core.fsmonitor. If a user opens an attacker-prepared repository whose preserved .git/config points core.fsmonitor to an attacker-controlled helper, Git can execute it outside Codex's command sandbox and without user approval.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: OpenAI Codex CLI for Windows, macOS, and Linux; Codex Desktop for Windows and macOS; requires repository copied or delivered with local .git/config intact.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a workspace-trust and local-agent containment failure where passive metadata inspection can cross into unsandboxed code execution.

upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General workspace-trust and coding-agent workflow guidance routes upstream; this CVE's security boundary remains local.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from NVD; vendor patch detail still needs reconciliation.
follow_up_actions: Check Codex release channels for version and mitigation mapping before durable synthesis.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenAI Codex Desktop can execute attacker-controlled Git attr/filter programs during workspace inspection
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD says Codex Desktop inspects Git metadata and working-tree status when a workspace opens. If preserved attacker-controlled .git/config sets attr.tree plus a clean or process filter, Git can run an attacker-controlled program outside Codex's command sandbox without workspace-trust prompt, command approval, model interaction, or further user action.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Codex Desktop for Windows and macOS; exploitation requires Git on PATH and a repository whose local Git configuration is preserved.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The record reinforces that AI coding agents need pre-model workspace trust gates and safe Git invocation boundaries, not only model-mediated command approvals.

upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General repository trust workflows route upstream; this security CVE stays local.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from NVD; ordinary Git clone not sufficient is explicitly part of the record.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, cluster with CVE-2026-19592 under local agent execution and workspace trust controls.

qualifying_findings.title: Hugging Face Transformers writes custom generate code before trust_remote_code consent
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD reports that Hugging Face Transformers versions 4.49.0 through 5.8.1 let GenerativePreTrainedModel.load_custom_generate() fetch and cache remote custom_generate/generate.py before the trust_remote_code consent check. Execution remains gated, but unauthorized files can persist in ~/.cache/huggingface/modules and collide with later trusted loads.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Hugging Face Transformers >= 4.49.0 and <= 5.8.1; dynamic_module_utils.py custom generate path.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model-loading consent must cover artifact fetch and persistence, not only execution; cached attacker code creates a supply-chain and stale-cache execution risk.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Hugging Face and Transformers entity context route upstream.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General dependency and model-loading workflow practice routes upstream; the security vulnerability remains local.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from NVD; patched version was not available in fetched record.

qualifying_findings.title: ModelScope unsafe YAML loader enables malicious model repository code execution
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD reports that ModelScope uses PyYAML's unsafe yaml.Loader to parse model configuration files, allowing Python object construction tags in malicious model repositories to execute arbitrary code when loaded.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: ModelScope model configuration parsing; affected versions not specified in fetched NVD output.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI model repositories are executable supply-chain surfaces when configuration parsing accepts unsafe object construction.

upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General dependency hygiene routes upstream; model repository RCE is local security material.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium-high confidence from NVD; fixed version and vendor advisory need follow-up.
follow_up_actions: Find vendor advisory or patch commit before durable fixed-version claims.

qualifying_findings.title: Elasticsearch machine learning component can execute code from crafted trained model artifacts
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD describes deserialization of untrusted data in Elasticsearch's machine learning component. A specially crafted trained model artifact can cause attacker-controlled logic to execute with a broader system-call surface than intended when an authenticated user has privileges to create and deploy trained models.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Elasticsearch machine learning component; trained model artifact deployment path.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model artifacts in production search and analytics stacks need provenance, deserialization controls, and least-privilege deployment rights.

qualifying_findings.title: Low-privileged Kibana Observability AI Assistant user can terminate the Kibana process
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD reports that an authenticated user with only low-privileged feature access for the Kibana Observability AI Assistant can submit a crafted request that triggers an unhandled error, terminates the Kibana process, and denies service to all users and spaces until restart.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Kibana Observability AI Assistant feature access path.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI assistant features inside operational platforms need resource and error isolation so low-privileged assistant access cannot become tenant-wide service impact.

qualifying_findings.title: Kibana AI Assistant Knowledge Base can cross user boundaries when usernames collide across realms
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD reports incorrect authorization in Kibana where two authenticated principals from different authentication realms sharing the same username could read, modify, and delete each other's private Elastic AI Assistant Knowledge Base entries.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Kibana Elastic AI Assistant Knowledge Base; multi-realm authentication configurations with same username values.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Assistant memory and knowledge stores require stable principal identity, not display-name or username-only matching across realms.

qualifying_findings.title: Low-privileged Kibana Agent Builder user can trigger unbounded memory consumption
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD reports an allocation-without-limits issue in Kibana where an authenticated user holding only low, read-level Agent Builder privileges can submit a crafted request that causes unbounded memory consumption, terminates the process, and denies service to all users.

qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent-builder control planes need strict resource guards and privilege-aware request limits even for read-level users.

qualifying_findings.title: runZero Platform MCP service fixes authorization bypass
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD says runZero resolved an authorization bypass in the Platform MCP service in version 5.1.260826.0. The issue is CWE-639 authorization bypass through user-controlled key, with low CVSS 3.5 but scope changed.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: runZero Platform MCP service before 5.1.260826.0; fixed in 5.1.260826.0.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP services that expose asset or security operations need key-bound authorization checks that cannot be steered by user-controlled identifiers.

qualifying_findings.title: NousResearch hermes-agent disclosures cover ACP prompt workflow DoS and MCP tool memory allocation
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD published two hermes-agent records. CVE-2026-84288 affects HermesACPAgent.prompt in acp_adapter/session.py and leads to remote denial of service through the ACP Prompt Workflow. CVE-2026-84289 affects list_tools in tools/mcp_tool.py and leads to uncontrolled memory allocation in the MCP Tool component. NVD says public exploits may be available and the vendor did not respond.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: public vulnerability database records and GitHub Advisory Database listing
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: NousResearch hermes-agent up to 0.18.2; ACP Prompt Workflow and MCP Tool components.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent frameworks that bridge ACP and MCP need bounded prompt and tool-list handling so remote inputs cannot degrade agent control-plane availability.

qualifying_findings.title: Support Genix AI Chatbot WordPress plugin can allow administrator account takeover
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD reports that Support Genix - Helpdesk, AI Chatbot, Knowledge Base & Customer Support Ticketing System for WordPress is vulnerable through version 1.4.52. A subscriber-level attacker with a legitimate guest ticket token can brute-force a weak site-wide AES-256-CBC key derived from low-entropy wp_rand values and activation timestamp, forge a token for an administrator-owned ticket, and cause wp_set_auth_cookie() to grant administrator access.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Support Genix WordPress plugin up to and including 1.4.52; guest_ticket_login() and public /sgnix/?p=<token> endpoint.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI chatbot and helpdesk plugins often touch customer support data and admin workflows; weak token cryptography can turn chatbot access into full site compromise.
